text:
marta: quick heads-up starting an int4 bring-up for Nucleus14B (hybrid llama/mistral headmap). short responses look ok but long 8k summaries show drift + periodic repetition around the kv wrap point (~2k tokens).

simon: can you share the exact reproduce command + a failing example?

marta: running locally: 
```
./bench_infer --model=nucleus14b --quant=int4 --seq_len=8192 --batch=1 --prompt-file=tests/long_summaries.txt --use-kvcache --cache-mode=streaming
```

marta: failing example (baseline vs our build):
- HF baseline: "In summary, the patient remained hemodynamically stable."
- Nucleus14B int4: "In summary, the patient remained hemodynamically stable. In summary, the patient remained..." repeats after token ~2048

jia: two quick checks: 1) tokenizer mapping (nucleus uses merged subword table + alternate BOS/EOS) 2) rotary mode (perhead vs perlayer). both can silently misalign kv indices.

nate: also check qpack version used during packaging. qpack v1 vs v2 changes weight layout ordering; if runtime assumes different head ordering the kv cache pointers will be off once wrap happens.

marta: ran tools/hf_to_redwood.py with --merge-unk true and compared first 200 token ids  they match, but ran tools/check_vocab_mapping.py and saw consistent +2 offset for token ids above 50265. oddly only the tail of vocab.

simon: that smells like an export script bug where sentinel offset wasn't applied for appended tokens. can you paste the tail of mapping for ids 50260-50270?

marta: attaching excerpt in log snippet (will paste soon).

ci-bot: packaging pipeline nucleus14b-int4 completed (sha: abc123) :white_check_mark:

jia: meanwhile try toggling runtime rope mode: REDWOOD_ROPE_MODE=perhead vs legacy. perhead will honor per-head phase scales; legacy applies same phase across heads. if model has mixed-rope that causes slow phase drift and then repetition.

marta: toggled to REDWOOD_ROPE_MODE=perhead  alignment improved up to ~2048 tokens but repetitions still occur after the cache wraps.

nate: try adding the kv-wrap diagnostic flag: --dump-kv-idx=2030-2060 to bench_infer. look for index jumps or duplicated indices when wrap happens.

marta: running that now. also starting a rebuild with qpack=v2 + kv-cache-wrap-fix branch (origin/kv-wrap-fix-2026).

simon: if qpack v2 + kv-wrap-fix fixes it we should schedule a canary on dedicated GPUs and extend the longctx eval set (include >4k, 6k samples). also add a regression test that tokenizes with nfkc normalization to catch diacritics-induced phase group shifts.

jia: good point about normalization. run tools/token_norm_check.py --mode=nfkc against the eval corpus. i've seen strange multi-codepoint sequences flip group membership and that interacts badly with per-head rotary if token boundaries change mid-sequence.

marta: added token norm check, running overnight int4 sweep with qpack=v2 + kv-wrap-fix + REDWOOD_ROPE_MODE=perhead. will post results in morning. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ci-bot: nightly eval triggered: nucleus14b-int4-longctx-sweep (job id: 2026-489)

simon: small addition  add a short test that forces kvcache to wrap multiple times in one sequence (e.g., repeat prompt to exceed 3x wrap) to catch head-order arithmetic errors deterministically.

marta: good idea. will add a synthetic test that loops a 2k token chunk 6x to force wrap and dump indices.

jia: one more diagnostic: dump sin/cos appliation per head for a few layers around the wrap to confirm mode applied consistently. a misapplied perlayer vs perhead switch shows up as headwise phase offsets.

marta: noted. summary of action items: 1) rebuild w/ qpack=v2 + origin/kv-wrap-fix, 2) run --dump-kv-idx around wrap, 3) run token_norm_check --mode=nfkc, 4) add synthetic repeated-wrap test, 5) run nightly int4 sweep + longctx ROUGE evals. will update tomorrow. :thumbsup:

simon: thanks  ping if logs show duplicated indices or unexpected jumps. we can roll back packaging strategy if needed.

marta: pinging @simon @jia @nate for any other ideas.
